corruptus

corruptus, corrupta, corruptum

adjective (participle of corrumpō)

spoiled, gone bad

In this lexicon

  • bad

    the recommended word · classical · Cato Agr. 3.2: nē corrumpātur; Cic. N.D. 2.20, of standing water (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • cernis ut ignāvum corrumpant ōtia corpus, ut capiant vitium, nī moveantur, aquae

    you see how idleness spoils a lazy body, and how water goes bad if it doesn’t moveOv. Pont. 1.5.5–6

    In the entry for bad

  • olea ubi lēcta siet, oleum fīat continuō, nē corrumpātur

    once the olives have been picked, the oil should be made at once, so that they don’t go badCato Agr. 3.2
